text: Setting clear goals at the start of a project is essential for success. A popular method is to use SMART goals, which means they should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. This helps avoid vague objectives that can confuse the team. Once the main goal is defined, it is useful to break the work into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that allow you to track progress and celebrate small wins along the way. Each milestone should have clear deliverables, meaning tangible outputs or results that can be reviewed. Finally, stakeholder alignment is crucial. This means ensuring that everyone involved, from clients to team members, agrees on the objectives and expectations. When all parties share the same vision, the project has a much higher chance of staying on track and finishing successfully.
